subject: Redevelopment of Cappy's Liquors and Monroe Muffler
overview: Alliance Residential Company presented a preliminary concept for an 8-story, 265-unit residential development at the intersection of Fellsway and Revere Beach Parkway. No formal applications have been filed as the developer is currently in a feasibility study period seeking neighborhood feedback.

items.title: Project Introduction and Site Context
items.summary: Kathleen Desmond and Mike Bejulian introduced a proposal to redevelop 573 Fellsway and 20 Revere Beach Parkway into a multifamily housing community.

items.title: Development Program and Concept Design
items.summary: The proposed eight-story building includes 265 rental units, 15% affordable housing, a central courtyard, and three levels of internal parking providing roughly one space per unit.

items.title: Site Access and Traffic Mitigation
items.summary: Developers proposed reducing the existing five curb cuts to a single entrance on Middlesex Avenue to eliminate cut-through traffic and prevent project-related vehicles from using Ninth Street.

items.title: Residential Concerns Regarding Ninth Street
items.summary: Neighbors raised concerns about existing congestion on the Ninth Street private way and requested the developer contribute to street improvements and traffic calming measures.

items.title: Environmental and Construction Impacts
items.summary: Residents questioned the team on rodent mitigation strategies and the use of seismic monitoring to protect adjacent properties from vibrations during the estimated 24-month construction period.

items.title: Commercial Use and Amenities
items.summary: The development team explained that retail space was excluded from the design to minimize traffic impacts and avoid the requirements of drive-through coffee tenants.

items.title: Parking Logistics and Unit Mix
items.summary: Developers discussed parking usage trends, potential shuttle services to Wellington Station, and a commitment to restricting residents from parking on nearby public streets via lease riders.

items.title: Project Feasibility and Next Steps
items.summary: The developer clarified that the project will be rental-only due to liability structures and noted that formal permit applications would likely follow the holiday season if they proceed.
